transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-23 15:00 UTC — Duration: 49m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (BluHarbor Head of Security), Liam Ortiz (Platform Lead), Priya Nair (Legal)
---
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Ethan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Aisha Rahman: Doing well, thanks. We've got about 45 minutes, want to run through our security posture, what we need to validate before any pilot.
00:13 Maya Chen: Perfect, that's exactly the agenda. Quick note: we'll send all compliance artifacts afterwards.
00:18 Ethan Park: Quick intro from me — I can dive into deployment models, network, and KMS questions.
00:24 Liam Ortiz: Great. We're focused on two things: one, how to keep PII out of the hosted platform, and two, set up RBAC so ops/dev teams have least privilege.
00:34 Priya Nair: And from legal I need to understand data retention guarantees and where logs live for audit.
00:40 Maya Chen: Understood. We can talk SOC 2, ISO, and our different hosting patterns — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem).
01:00 Aisha Rahman: Can you confirm Redwood has SOC2 Type II? And do you have an ISO cert?
01:05 Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II in 2025 — we will share the report summary. ISO 27001 is in progress, expecting certification early 2027 — we'll share the scope doc.
01:20 Aisha Rahman: Okay, timeline noted. What's the difference from a compliance perspective between Hosted and Dedicated?
01:28 Ethan Park: Hosted is our managed multi-tenant API, logs are retained in our control plane; for Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and logical isolation — we can front the data plane in a VPC and provide tighter network controls and longer retention per contract; Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
01:48 Liam Ortiz: For Dedicated, do we get an option for customer-managed KMS? We need BYOK for keys at rest.
01:54 Ethan Park: Yes, Dedicated and Private support BYOK via KMS integrations. We have docs for AWS KMS and GCP KMS; HSM integrations available for enterprise via our support channel. There's also an option to use Redwood-managed keys if you can't manage keys yourself.
02:10 Aisha Rahman: How are audit logs surfaced? We need token-level request logs with user/principal, model used, prompt hash, and response hash for forensics. Retention mandated is 5 years for us.
02:22 Maya Chen: We emit per-request audit events — user principal, model, route, latency, error codes, and we can include request/response metadata. Full verbatim storage is opt-in; by default we store metadata and hashes. Retention is contract configurable; 5 years is doable via an add-on retention tier.
02:42 Priya Nair: Where are the logs stored — in Redwood cloud region, or can they ship to our S3?
02:48 Ethan Park: For Dedicated/Private, we can forward logs to your S3 or SIEM (via S3 or syslog). Hosted logs live in our region but we support log export. For PII concerns, we recommend log shipping to your tenant S3.
03:10 Liam Ortiz: About SSO — we run Okta and need SAML + SCIM for user provisioning and groups mapping to RBAC. How do we map Okta groups to Redwood roles?
03:18 Ethan Park: We support SAML SSO for auth and SCIM for provisioning. Group-to-role mapping is configurable in the console or via API; we support role templates like viewer, editor, admin, and can create custom roles to enforce least privilege.
03:34 Aisha Rahman: Do you support fine-grained RBAC per model or per route? We want only certain teams to call production models.
03:40 Ethan Park: Yes, RBAC can be scoped to routes, models, and projects. You can bind a role to a group that only has access to a production model endpoint.
03:50 Maya Chen: There's also token scoping — API keys can be scoped to only generate embeddings or only call a particular model.
04:00 Priya Nair: Encryption at rest — is data encrypted with customer keys always, or only for certain deployment modes?
04:06 Ethan Park: For Hosted, by default we encrypt at rest with Redwood-managed keys; Dedicated and Private offer BYOK. For enterprise with stricter controls, we enable customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys.
04:20 Liam Ortiz: What about KV cache and intermediate cache — is that encrypted as well? We can't have unencrypted intermediate state with PII.
04:27 Ethan Park: All KV cache and prefix caches can be encrypted when the deployment uses customer-managed KMS — the runtime is configured to encrypt cache blobs. We'll need to map exactly what you consider PII so we can recommend cache exclusions.
04:40 Aisha Rahman: Are there controls to scrub prompts or redact PII before sending to the model?
04:46 Ethan Park: We provide middleware hooks and pre-send filters; customers often run a scrub step in their app or use Redwood's pre-processing plugin to redact or replace PII. That can run in your VPC for Private deployments.
05:00 Maya Chen: On the legal side, we have DPA and standard data processing terms — we'll share the current DPA.
05:05 Priya Nair: Please do. Also need to confirm certifications required for our internal auditors — they will want the SOC2 bridge and any complementary evidence.
05:14 Maya Chen: We'll include a SOC2 bridge and our recent penetration test summary.
05:21 Liam Ortiz: Network setup — for Dedicated, do you support private endpoints or VPC peering? We prefer no public internet egress for inference traffic.
05:28 Ethan Park: Dedicated supports private VPC peering, Private deployments can be fully on-prem or inside your cloud VPC with no internet egress. For hosted, we can support private endpoints with MTLS in some cases, but hosted is primarily public endpoints with TLS.
05:42 Aisha Rahman: Incident response — do you provide breach notification SLA and runbooks?
05:48 Maya Chen: Yes, enterprise contracts include incident notification timelines. We maintain an incident runbook and can provide details on escalation contacts.
06:00 Priya Nair: For retention policy, you said retention is configurable — what's the default for hosted?
06:06 Maya Chen: Default is 90 days for metadata and 30 days for raw content unless opted-in. We can extend to 5 years with dedicated retention add-on for Dedicated/Private.
06:20 Liam Ortiz: Any red flags around exporting data for EU residency? We're global and need EU data residency to keep logs and data in eu-west region.
06:27 Ethan Park: We support region restriction for Dedicated and Private — you can pin region for both compute and control plane; hosted customers can request region-specific hosting and we have EU regions with data residency controls for enterprise plans.
06:46 Aisha Rahman: What's the encryption algorithm and key rotation policy?
06:50 Ethan Park: We use AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ for transit. For customers using our KMS, keys are rotated annually; for BYOK you control rotation per your KMS policies.
07:05 Priya Nair: Is there hardware-backed key protection (HSM)?
07:08 Ethan Park: Yes, we integrate with HSM-backed KMS providers and can support FIPS/HSM modules for keys on request.
07:16 Liam Ortiz: About logs integrity — can you sign or hash logs to prove they weren't tampered with?
07:22 Ethan Park: We support log hashing and can ship signed manifests. For high-assurance customers we can configure append-only log stores in your S3 with lifecycle and object lock.
07:36 Aisha Rahman: Any PII minimization recommended patterns? We want to avoid sending raw customer PII into prompts.
07:42 Ethan Park: Common patterns: client-side tokenization/redaction, pseudonymization, and encrypting sensitive fields before sending. Also use model hallucination detection with eval sets to flag sensitive outputs.
07:58 Maya Chen: Quick question from our side — are you leaning to Hosted to start or jumping straight to Dedicated/Private?
08:05 Liam Ortiz: We're evaluating a pilot — probably Dedicated to start but want to validate security first. Hosted is attractive for speed but our compliance team nervous about multi-tenant.
08:15 Aisha Rahman: Yes, Dedicated with BYOK and log shipping to our S3 would be acceptable if we get SOC2 artifacts and can run a short pen test or benchmark.
08:26 Ethan Park: We can arrange a scoped pen test or a bench of the inference path in a Dedicated environment. We'll also provide a readiness checklist.
08:36 Priya Nair: Contractually, we may need indemnities for data exfiltration. We'll flag that for legal but need to see DPA.
08:44 Maya Chen: Noted — we'll push DPA and indemnity language to you.
08:48 Aisha Rahman: On the operational side, can we set rate limits and quotas per API key to control blast radius?
08:54 Ethan Park: Absolutely, per-token quotas, burst controls, and per-key rate limits are configurable. You can also enforce per-route guardrails.
09:05 Liam Ortiz: Can we get token-level billing breakdowns to map cost to teams?
09:10 Maya Chen: Yes, our console provides token cost breakdown per key/route and per model. Redwood Optimize will also suggest batch/quantization options for cost savings.
09:24 Aisha Rahman: For model version pinning and rollouts — how are rollbacks handled if a model regression occurs?
09:30 Ethan Park: We support canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant on errors or QoS degradation. We also keep model versioning and audit trails.
09:44 Priya Nair: A few clarifying Qs from legal: do you sub-processors, and if so what's your list?
09:49 Maya Chen: Yes, we have subprocessors — infra cloud providers and monitoring/CDN partners. We'll share the current subprocessor list and the process for change notification.
09:58 Aisha Rahman: For the SOC2 bridge, can we request more granular control evidence around access logs for the control plane?
10:04 Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide control plane access logs and privileged access reviews for the period covered by the SOC2.
10:14 Liam Ortiz: Any concerns about model artifacts being stored long-term? For example, embeddings that might be persisted — are those under the same retention?
10:21 Ethan Park: Embeddings are treated as user data — retention follows the configured policy. You can opt to not persist embeddings or to encrypt them with your KMS.
10:32 Aisha Rahman: Do you have data deletion guarantees (time to delete) once we request a purge?
10:38 Ethan Park: Deletions are performed and propagated within our data plane; for Hosted we commit to 30 days for full purge unless otherwise contracted. For Dedicated/Private we can guarantee shorter SLAs per contract.
10:50 Priya Nain (sic): typo in transcript: Priya Nair said earlier: Any contractual obligations for law enforcement requests?
10:58 Maya Chen: We notify customers of lawful requests when permitted and have a process in our DPA. For Private deployments under your control, that is your responsibility.
11:12 Aisha Rahman: Ok, that's useful.
11:16 Ethan Park: We should follow up with a tech appendix showing network diagrams for Dedicated & Private, and a sample KMS config.
11:24 Maya Chen: Agree. For next steps we'll send the SOC2 and DPA, sizing for Dedicated, and propose a date for the technical deep dive.
11:32 Liam Ortiz: Sounds good. Also want an estimate for retention add-on costs for 5-year storage.
11:38 Maya Chen: We'll include that in the pricing pack.
11:43 Aisha Rahman: One last ask — can Redwood support a small pilot where we run a subset of traffic through Dedicated and keep non-sensitive calls on Hosted?
11:51 Ethan Park: Yes, hybrid routing is supported; policy-based routing can route by customer, route, or model. That pattern is common for staged migrations.
12:00 Maya Chen: Great; thank you all. We'll put the notes and artifacts in an email follow-up.
12:06 Priya Nair: Thanks.
12:08 Liam Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
12:10 Aisha Rahman: Bye.
---
End of transcript. Some ASR errors noted: 'Priya Nain' typo and occasional acronyms mis-heard (KMS as K-M-S, HSM as H-S-M).
